chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Talha al-Nahdi, from Sawrat ibn Kuleyb, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man leaves his house intending to go to the mosque or for a need, and a man meets him or follows him, beats him, and takes his clothes.
He (peace be upon him) said: What do the people around you say about it? I said: They say this is an open violation, but rather the warrior (muharib) is in the towns of the polytheists.
He (peace be upon him) said: Which is greater in sanctity, the house of Islam or the house of polytheism? I said: The house of Islam.
He (peace be upon him) said: These are the ones subject to this Verse: 'The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger'... up to the end of the Verse.

key_terms.إِنَّما جَزاءُ الَّذِينَ يُحارِبُونَ الل: The recompense of those who wage war against Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for someone who attacks and robs another person in a Muslim town?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration in the chapter on Hadd al-Muharibah, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the prevailing view that 'muharibah' (waging war) was restricted to polytheist territories, extending it to Dar al-Islam. By citing Quran 5:33, the Imam establishes that individual highway robbery or assault in Muslim lands carries the same severe legal weight as the broader concept of rebellion against divine authority, emphasizing the sanctity of public safety in Islamic governance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Talha Al Nahdy, from Sowrat Bin Kuleyb who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man comes out from his house intending (to go to) the Masjid, or he intends the need, so he meets a man or he is followed by him, and he beats him up and takes his clothes’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Which thing are they saying with regards to it, the ones who are around you?’ I said, ‘They are saying, ‘This is an open violation, but rather the warrior is in the town of the Polytheists’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Which one is greater in sanctity, the house of Al-Islam or the house of the Polytheism?’ I said, ‘The house of Al-Islam’.
Heasws said: ‘These are the ones who are rightful of this Verse [5:33] But rather, the Recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Rasool – up to the end of the Verse’.
